subject: Request: token-pathway visibility + drillable model traces
messages:
From: Sam Truong <sam.truong@veridianhealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: platform@veridianhealth.com
Date: 2028-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Token-level cost visibility request – example traces attached

Hi Olga,

Quick note from the platform team at Veridian — we’re seeing intermittent spikes in per-call billing that are hard to explain from the dashboard. The per-endpoint tiles show overall token spend, but we can’t map expensive requests back to the specific model path or token phase (prompt vs generation vs post-processing).

I attached a small CSV with sampled request IDs and a screenshot of a trace from this morning. Can Redwood provide a drillable view that shows:
- Token counts split by phase (client prompt / prefix cache / generation / post-process)
- Which model variant and quantization profile served the request
- Per-token timing breakdown so we can spot hotspots (e.g., attention-heavy sequences)

This would help us correlate our application-side batching changes with actual per-token economics. We’d like to scope a short proof-of-concept before the end of the month.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if that helps.

—Sam
Sam Truong
Platform Lead, Veridian Health
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Sam Truong <sam.truong@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-18T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Token-level cost visibility request – example traces attached

Hi Sam — thanks for the sample and the clear asks.

We can definitely build a focused, drillable view that ties token phases to cost and latency. Proposal for an initial scope (30% prototype):
1) Request-level breakdown: split tokens into prompt / prefix (KV cache hits) / generation / post-process with cost attribution.
2) Model metadata: show model name, variant, quantization and region that served each request.
3) Lightweight trace visualization: per-token time heatmap and top-3 expensive layers for flagged requests.

Questions for scoping:
- Do you need continuous sampling (1% of traffic) or ad-hoc exports from your selected time windows?
- Which SLA for latency should we consider when enabling per-token traces (they add overhead)?

Looping in Marissa and Ben to estimate UI effort and telemetry work. I’ll volunteer to drive the mutual action plan and get a quick prototype up in staging.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior PM, Console & Observability
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, Sam Truong <sam.truong@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Token-level cost visibility request – example traces attached

Thanks, Olga. A few quick notes from the UI/UX side:
- Preferred surface: add a linked panel from the existing Endpoint detail page (so customers can click a request id and open the token-pathway pane). This keeps navigation minimal.
- Wireframe ask: we’ll deliver a minimal mock (header + stacked token bars + model metadata + download CSV) — should be ~2 screens.
- Export: include a CSV/NDJSON export for sampled sessions (useful for Veridian’s side-by-side analysis).

For prioritization: if Sam wants a 30%-prototype by end of month, we need telemetry payloads defined today so infra can enable sampling in staging. Olga — can you confirm sampling approach?

—Marissa
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Sam Truong <sam.truong@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Token-level cost visibility request – example traces attached

Quick infra note: per-token timing at production scale is expensive if enabled for all traffic. Recommend:
- Stage 1 (PoC): 0.5% sampling for selected endpoints, write traces to a compressed S3 path + index minimal metadata in ES for quick lookup.
- Stage 2 (Ops): on-demand capture (toggleable from console) for a request id with a short TTL.

I’ll create the tracing toggle and S3 schema; need the list of fields Marissa needs in the export (token phase, token index, ms per-token, model_variant, quantized_bits).

—Ben
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Sam Truong <sam.truong@veridianhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Token-level cost visibility request – example traces attached

All — great alignment. Next steps:
1) Marissa will ship a simple mock today (link below) so Veridian can confirm UX.
2) Ben will enable 0.5% sampling in staging and push schema (expected by EOD today).
3) Olga to open a short-lived Jira (JIRA-OBS-4123) and draft the mutual action plan. Sam — once you confirm you’re OK with 0.5% sampling and the fields below we’ll schedule a 30–45m sync to review the prototype.

Telemetry export fields (initial): request_id, timestamp, endpoint, customer_tenant, model_variant, quantized_bits, token_phase, token_index, token_text_omitted_flag, ms_per_token, cost_estimate_usd

Links:
- Mock (Marissa): https://drive.google.com/mock-token-pathway
- Sampling schema (Ben): https://drive.google.com/schemas/traces-sampling
- HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/98765/company/Veridian

Attachments: token-pathway-sample.csv, trace-screenshot-annotated.png

Olga
Senior PM, Console & Observability
Redwood Inference
